title: Ruscocunks Creek
summary: Ruscocunks is recorded as a creek east of Mastic Neck in the Town of Brookhaven.
history_content: The name appears in a December 20, 1693 deed from William Smith to John Wood. Ruscocunks is treated as a variation sharing its derivation with Areshunk, while the place itself is identified as a creek east of Mastic Neck.
translation_content:
The name is connected with Areshunk and the Native personal name Warishone or Worison. That derivation is linked with a word meaning "to forget" or "the forgetter."

Why Place Names Matter

“Until it is given a name, a particular place is only a memory in someone’s mind. Once it is named, the memory can be shared with other people: the place becomes part of human legacy.”

— Béatrice Collignon, Knowing Places: The Innunnait, Landscapes and the Environment (2006), p. 101; reproduced in Sarah Simpkin, “Evaluating the inclusion of Inuvialuktun place names in online maps” (2023), p. 8
preservation_content: Ruscocunks connects a creek name in southeastern Brookhaven with Native personal naming and seventeenth-century land records. Keeping it distinct from Areshunk preserves the local geography while noting the shared derivation.
